text: Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error A two-dimensional scalar conservation law transports a slotted disk in a prescribed rigid-rotation velocity. Compare donor-cell upwinding and minmod MUSCL with the same SSPRK(3,3), checking full-turn mass, bounds, shape error and dependence on grid placement and initial angle. The base refinements use64²,128² and256² cells, with separate placement and initial-angle diagnostics at64². These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-zalesak-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error Rotate a slotted disk through one full turn with an actual 2D finite-volume solver, comparing donor-cell and minmod MUSCL. Eight runs combine three grids with half-cell-center and 45-degree-start probes; measure conservation, bounds at every SSP stage, shape error and slot filling. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Fix the dimensionless unit square, rotation center(.5,.5), disk center(.5,.75), radius.15, slot width.05/top y=.85, angular speed1, T=2pi and64²/128²/256² cells. The body is1 and exterior/slot0. Periodic normal face velocities match; the exact compact support stays away from the boundary. The periodic extension has a tangential-velocity seam, and diffusive tails reaching its fixed-width boundary band are measured. Editorial clarification This is scalar transport in a prescribed divergence-free rotation, not Euler-fluid evolution. It uses a Zalesak-type slotted-disk shape test without claiming implementation of Zalesak’s FCT algorithm. Pointwise indicator values and geometric conserved cell means are distinguished; numerical tails near periodic boundaries are also measured. The initial32²/64²/128² series passed26 tests and156/158 gates, but its finest relative L1 was about1.11675 for donor-cell(limit1.0) and.6023 for MUSCL(limit.55), so it failed. Retain all original inputs,criteria,fields and failed decisions. A new pre-execution contract refines the base series to64²/128²/256² without changing acceptance thresholds, flux algorithms or the26 tests. Revision 2 passed all 26 tests and all 158 gates over eight runs; tests plus the fixed-input driver took about 19.58 seconds within one 120-second budget. At N=256 the relative L1 errors are about 0.932256 for donor-cell and 0.394271 for MUSCL (ratio about 0.423); the maximum absolute mass change over all runs is about 8.90e-15. Recorded stage bounds are 0 to 1, including initial states, but bounds alone do not establish accurate slot preservation. The inner empty-slot probe weights the piecewise-constant cell-mean field; it is not a point value of the continuum solution. Mixed reference cells create a projection baseline, so numerical mean, reference mean and their excess are stored separately. At N=256 the excesses are about 0.63465 and 0.36501 for donor-cell/MUSCL, showing substantial remaining diffusion. At N=64 the MUSCL slot excess can exceed donor-cell, so no uniform improvement across every metric and grid is claimed. The N=256 mass fractions in the fixed-width 0.05 boundary band are about 0.0178615/0.000243761 for donor-cell/MUSCL. The compact exact field vanishes there; these periodic-boundary tails remain visible in the diagnostics. Adopted numerical method Use analytic divergence-free normal face averages and one shared upwind flux per interface. Both piecewise-constant donor-cell and mean-preserving directional-minmod MUSCL use SSPRK(3,3). The four face-midpoint mean equals the cell mean; individual outgoing-face Courant<=1/4 gives a convex FE update. Check the actual .20 bound at every stage. Independent circle/convex-polygon intersection means are qualified against SciPy vertical-slice quadrature, total area and first moments. Also check quarter/half/three-quarter-turn errors and centroids so a wrong direction or speed cannot hide behind a full-turn return. Verification limits and failures This is an isolated0–1 standard slotted body with periodic boundaries. It does not implement Zalesak FCT, reproduce the original paper’s grid/boundaries or the entire Firedrake bell/cone/background demonstration. The inner-slot diagnostic area-weights piecewise-constant means over a fixed rectangle. Coarse exact cell projection can already give a nonzero baseline, which is reported separately from excess numerical filling. Two center/orientation probes do not establish universal isotropy, perfect shape retention or a maximum principle for arbitrary flows. Tiny geometric-area roundoff handling is distinguished from the absence of transported-state clipping. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded.
